title.en: Mechanism of evolution and Hardy–Weinberg principle

heading.en: When does a population stop changing?

hook.en: If nothing disturbs a population, its allele frequencies stay the same generation after generation. *Evolution* is what happens when something disturbs that balance.
hook.kn: ಏನೂ ಅಡ್ಡಿಯಾಗದಿದ್ದರೆ ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ ಅಲೀಲ್ ಆವರ್ತನಗಳು ಪೀಳಿಗೆಯಿಂದ ಪೀಳಿಗೆಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಆ ಸಮತೋಲನ ಕದಡಿದಾಗ ವಿಕಾಸ ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: In a population, allele frequencies are stable and constant from generation to generation; the gene pool remains constant. This is genetic equilibrium. If p and q are the frequencies of two alleles, then p + q = 1 and the genotype frequencies are p², 2pq and q², which add up to 1. When the measured frequencies differ from these expected values, the difference shows the extent of evolutionary change.
body.kn: ಹಾರ್ಡಿ–ವೈನ್‌ಬರ್ಗ್ ತತ್ವ: ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅಲೀಲ್ ಆವರ್ತನಗಳು ಸ್ಥಿರವಾಗಿರುತ್ತವೆ. p + q = 1; p² + 2pq + q² = 1. ಇದರಿಂದ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ಕಂಡರೆ ವಿಕಾಸ ಆಗುತ್ತಿದೆ.

say.en: In a population, allele frequencies are stable and constant from generation to generation; the gene pool remains constant. This is genetic equilibrium. If p and q are the frequencies of two alleles, then p plus q equals 1 and the genotype frequencies are p squared, 2pq and q squared, which add up to 1. When the measured frequencies differ from these expected values, the difference shows the extent of evolutionary change.
say.kn: ಹಾರ್ಡಿ-ವೈನ್‌ಬರ್ಗ್ ತತ್ವ: ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅಲೀಲ್ ಆವರ್ತನಗಳು ಸ್ಥಿರವಾಗಿರುತ್ತವೆ. p plus q equals 1; p squared plus 2pq plus q squared equals 1. ಇದರಿಂದ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ಕಂಡರೆ ವಿಕಾಸ ಆಗುತ್ತಿದೆ.

say.en: p squared plus 2pq plus q squared equals 1.
Deviation equals evolution.
If p and q are the frequencies of two alleles, p plus q is 1. Squaring gives the genotype frequencies: p squared, 2pq and q squared.
Example: if 16 percent are aa, q squared is 0.16, so q is 0.4 and p is 0.6. Carriers, 2pq, are 0.48: almost half the population.
Five factors disturb this equilibrium. When they act, allele frequencies change: that is evolution.
Stabilising selection favours the mean: the curve gets taller and narrower.
Directional selection favours one end: the curve shifts.
Disruptive selection favours both ends: the curve splits into two peaks.
Board: Hardy-Weinberg and natural selection.

narration.en: Set the starting frequency of the recessive allele and step through the generations. First with no selection, then with every aa individual removed before breeding.
narration.kn: ಹಾರ್ಡಿ–ವೈನ್‌ಬರ್ಗ್, ನಂತರ ಆಯ್ಕೆ. ಸ್ಲೈಡರ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಸರಿಸಿ, ಓದುಗಳು ಹೇಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂದು ಗಮನಿಸಿ.

caption.en: With no selection, allele frequencies stay the same every generation and the genotypes stay at p², 2pq and q². If every aa individual fails to breed, q falls as q0/(1 + n q0): fast at first, then very slowly, because rare a alleles hide in Aa carriers.
caption.kn: ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಆಲೀಲ್ ಆವರ್ತನಗಳು ಪ್ರತಿ ಪೀಳಿಗೆಯಲ್ಲೂ ಸ್ಥಿರ: p², 2pq, q². ಎಲ್ಲ aa ವ್ಯಕ್ತಿಗಳು ಸಂತಾನ ಮಾಡದಿದ್ದರೆ q = q0/(1 + n q0): ಮೊದಲು ವೇಗ, ನಂತರ ತುಂಬಾ ನಿಧಾನ, ಏಕೆಂದರೆ ಅಪರೂಪದ a ಆಲೀಲ್‌ಗಳು Aa ವಾಹಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅಡಗಿರುತ್ತವೆ.

tryThis.en: With selection against aa, how many generations halve q from 0.5? From 0.1?

body.en: Five *factors* affect Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium: gene migration or gene flow, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination and natural selection. When genes move between populations, frequencies change (gene flow); if the change happens by chance it is genetic drift. Sometimes the change is so large that a few founders form a different population: the founder effect. Natural selection can be stabilising (more individuals take the mean value), directional (more take a value other than the mean) or disruptive (more individuals at both ends of the distribution).
body.kn: ಸಮತೋಲನವನ್ನು ಐದು ಅಂಶಗಳು ಕದಡುತ್ತವೆ: ಜೀನ್ ಪ್ರವಾಹ, ಆನುವಂಶಿಕ ದಿಕ್ಚ್ಯುತಿ, ಉತ್ಪರಿವರ್ತನೆ, ಪುನರ್ಸಂಯೋಜನೆ ಮತ್ತು ನೈಸರ್ಗಿಕ ಆಯ್ಕೆ. ನೈಸರ್ಗಿಕ ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಸ್ಥಿರಗೊಳಿಸುವ, ದಿಕ್ಕಿನ ಅಥವಾ ವಿಚ್ಛೇದಕ ಆಗಿರಬಹುದು.

say.en: ~15 mya — Dryopithecus (more ape-like) and Ramapithecus (more man-like); Ramapithecus fossils found in the Siwalik hills of India and Pakistan. ~2 mya — Australopithecines in East African grasslands; hunted with stone weapons, ate fruit.

problem.en: In a population in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, 16% of individuals show a recessive trait (aa). Find p, q and the percentage of carriers (Aa).

narration.en: Let us work this out together. In a population in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, 16% of individuals show a recessive trait (aa). Find p, q and the percentage of carriers (Aa).

say.en: Let us work this out together. In a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 16 percent of individuals show a recessive trait aa. Find p, q and the percentage of carriers Aa.
q squared equals 0.16, so q equals the square root of 0.16 equals 0.4.
p equals 1 - q equals 0.6.
Carriers equals 2pq equals 2 times 0.6 times 0.4 equals 0.48.
So the answer is q equals 0.4, p equals 0.6, carriers equals 48 percent.

problem.en: In a population of 1000, 360 are AA, 480 are Aa and 160 are aa. Find the frequency of allele A.

steps.en: Each person has two alleles: total = 2000.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. In a population of 1000, 360 are AA, 480 are Aa and 160 are aa. Find the frequency of allele A.

say.en: Let us work this out together. In a population of 1000, 360 are AA, 480 are Aa and 160 are aa. Find the frequency of allele A.
Each person has two alleles: total equals 2000.
A alleles equals 2 times 360 plus 480 equals 1200.
p equals 1200 divided by 2000 equals 0.6.
So the answer is pA equals 0.6.

body.en: In Hardy–Weinberg problems the recessive phenotype gives q² directly. Take its square root to get q, then p = 1 − q, then carriers = 2pq.
